title: GIVA pulled its Raksha Bandhan ad, and Kriti Sanon is still answering for it
body: Kriti Sanon spoke on Kareena Kapoor Khan's show 'What Women Want' about the backlash to her GIVA jewellery ad. The ad showed her in a bralette-style blouse with a cape and draped skirt, and some users said the outfit was unsuitable for the festival. Sanon said trolls also posted abusive comments on her parents' and sister's social media posts. She said the row reflects how women are judged over small things. Kangana Ranaut had called the ad 'intentionally creepy'. The page carries no statistics.

title: NPCI postpones the 0.4% UPI merchant fee after shopkeeper pushback
body: NPCI said it was delaying the merchant fee planned for October 15 because of the festive shopping season. The page says the rollout will now happen after Diwali, with no new date given. The fee was 0.4% on eligible merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300. Merchants receiving less than ₹100,000 a month through UPI were exempt. Retailers and petrol pump operators opposed it, and some warned they could stop accepting UPI. Banks and payment firms say they need a way to recover UPI's running costs, which the page puts at about ₹200 billion a year.

title: October 1 brings dearer TVs, ACs and fridges, plus fewer free SBI ATM withdrawals
body: Prices of TVs, air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines were set to rise 5% to 8% from October 1, ahead of the festive sales. The page's example is that a ₹50,000 TV would cost ₹2,500 to ₹4,000 more. From October 1, free SBI salary-account withdrawals at other banks' ATMs fall from 10 to five a month. The charge beyond the free limit is ₹15 plus GST per transaction. The page also flags a possible RBI rate decision on October 7 and the UPI merchant fee. It quotes no consumers; it frames the changes as a squeeze on household budgets.

title: Quick-commerce fees are quietly stretching festive budgets, says LocalCircles
body: A LocalCircles study found that 60% of quick-commerce users say delivery, handling and small-cart fees often push their final bill above what they expected: 42% very often, 18% often and 12% sometimes. For festive shopping, 71% will pick a platform on price or value, 65% on quality and 43% on low or no extra charges. Only 22% cite fast delivery. The study drew over 2,04,000 responses across 130 districts. Amazon Now and Zepto scored highest overall, and Blinkit scored highest on speed. The page's advice is to compare the final checkout total, not the listing price.

title: Mumbai FDA action on quick-commerce warehouses puts product quality in focus before Diwali
body: Maharashtra's FDA acted against quick-commerce warehouses in Malad West and Bhiwandi over expired and damaged food. It also suspended food licences of several stores and warehouses after finding cockroaches in fresh produce. A related headline mentions a Blinkit Bhiwandi licence suspension over ₹32.71 lakh of expired stock. In a LocalCircles survey of 27,000+ Mumbai respondents, 62% put product quality first and 61% put price first. 61% said fees often push their bill higher than expected. The page quotes no company or official reaction.

title: OPPO raises A6x prices by up to ₹2,000, pushing the entry 5G phone past ₹20,000
body: OPPO raised A6x prices in India by up to ₹2,000. The 4GB+64GB model went from ₹19,999 to ₹20,999, the 4GB+128GB from ₹23,999 to ₹25,999, and the 6GB+128GB from ₹26,999 to ₹28,999. The page says buyers of budget 5G phones may need to raise their budgets. It also says 5G phones under ₹20,000 could get harder to find next year. It carries no quotes from users or OPPO, and says the hike alone does not confirm other brands will follow.

title: Is outrage rewriting the rules of festive advertising?
body: The piece looks at how festive ads such as Tanishq's Ekatvam, Fabindia's Jashn-e-Riwaaz, Surf Excel, Mohey Manyavar and GIVA's Raksha Bandhan film keep drawing online backlash, boycott calls and withdrawals. Marketers disagree on the response. Shradha Agarwal says 'Online backlash can be loud without necessarily reflecting what most consumers think.' Binaifer Dulani says audiences may want festivals 'to simply be festivals'. Pritha Jha warns that pulling ads under intimidation rewards such tactics. The page has no statistics.

title: Festive sales: shoppers log in but hold back on big-ticket purchases
body: Redseer put first-leg online GMV (Oct 8–18) at $7-8 Bn, with nearly 100 Mn shoppers placing more than 350 Mn orders. Datum put online sales at ₹29,800-₹30,900 Cr, down 7-10% from ₹33,200 Cr a year earlier. Card payment value on October 9 fell 18% to ₹6,594 Cr. Counterpoint said smartphone sales fell 16% in the first three days. LocalCircles expects urban households to spend ₹1.97 Lakh Cr on festive discretionary items, down 6%. Its founder Sachin Taparia said 'Household earnings are not rising, and inflation continues to rise.' The page also cites an Economic Times report that festive discounts were 35-40% lower than last year.

title: Maruti raises Ertiga prices as demand stays strong
body: Maruti raised prices on some Ertiga variants in October 2026. The ZXi Plus petrol manual and automatic went up ₹10,000 each, to ₹11.79 lakh and ₹13.14 lakh. The Tour M petrol manual and CNG manual rose ₹2,500 each. Other variants are unchanged, and the range now runs from ₹8.90 lakh to ₹13.14 lakh. The page ties the revision to September sales of 16,911 units, up about 39.6% from 12,115 a year earlier. It carries no buyer reactions.

title: Gold sales projected to fall 11% in October as record prices bite
body: Retail gold sales volume is projected to fall 11% in October from a year earlier. 24-karat gold is near Rs 143,000 per 10 grams on MCX, roughly 10% higher than a year ago. Middle-income households are buying smaller amounts or delaying purchases in the hope of a price correction. Jewellers are offering discounts on making charges, gold-rate protection schemes and old-gold exchange bonuses. The India Bullion and Jewellers Association says activity has improved slightly since September, but the year-on-year gap remains a concern.

title: Gold and silver slip from early-October highs as Dhanteras nears
body: 24K gold opened October at ₹1,47,904 per 10g, hit a monthly high of ₹1,51,507 and bottomed at ₹1,42,044 on October 23. Most cities were around ₹1,43,290 later in the month. Silver fell about 14%, from near ₹2.26 lakh to about ₹1.94 lakh per kg. Dhanteras is on November 6 and Diwali on November 8. The World Gold Council reported early signs of stronger seasonal demand. The page says high prices last year likely cut Dhanteras sales volumes by about 15%, and says the lower prices favour physical buyers.

title: Commercial LPG up for a second month; household cylinders unchanged
body: 19 kg commercial LPG rose by Rs 62.50 to Rs 71.50 per cylinder on October 1. Delhi is now Rs 2,810 and Patna is the highest at Rs 3,100.50. The domestic 14.2 kg cylinder did not change: Delhi Rs 942 and Mumbai Rs 941.50. The page says domestic prices have been unchanged since June 7, 2026. It links the rise to higher crude and shipping disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent near $108. The page has no consumer reactions, but commercial LPG costs matter to small eateries and their customers.

title: InnoData lays off nearly 550 employees in India, job cuts reported in the Philippines
body: InnoData reportedly laid off nearly 550 employees in India on 26 October 2026. Staff lost access to company systems during the workday, and termination emails then reached their personal accounts. The email cited a 'reduced business assignment' and said it was 'not related to your individual performance'. One employee said a WhatsApp group reached 'almost 500 people' by late evening. Another described colleagues as 'all clueless and in a state of panic'. Workers also could not download payslips because HR payroll app access was revoked. The company has not publicly confirmed the totals.

title: Amazon layoffs hit India again: what severance pay can sacked workers expect
body: Amazon is cutting 'fewer than 1,000 employees' in its Stores division. Marketplace support, customer service and engineering teams in India and the UK are affected. This is part of about 30,000 corporate cuts that began in late 2025. Affected staff shared worries on an internal Slack channel, mainly about severance and the availability of internal job postings. Former employees estimate severance at one week of base pay for every six months of service. The article's example is 3 years of service on a ₹1,60,000 monthly base, which would give a lump sum of ₹2,40,000. A separate Inc42 report dated 09 Oct'26 says ET, citing sources, put the India impact at at least 100 employees; Amazon has not disclosed the Indian number.

title: TCS adds 4,258 employees in Q2, third straight quarter of headcount addition
body: TCS added a net 4,258 employees in the September 2026 quarter, taking headcount to 598,056. This is the third consecutive quarter of net growth, after a heavy FY26 in which the page says headcount fell by over 23,000. Trailing 12-month attrition was 13.3%, down from 13.6% the previous quarter. TCS issued about 25,000 fresher offers at the start of FY27. Its AI revenue was annualised at $3.1 billion, above 10% of total revenue. The CHRO said 'attrition remained stable at 13.3%'. For IT workers who watched TCS shrink last year, the rebound is a notable change, though hiring is described as demand-led.

title: India's white-collar hiring rises 2% in September as AI/ML hiring jumps 20%
body: The Naukri JobSpeak Index rose to 3,053 in September 2026 from 3,002 a year earlier, a 2% increase. AI/ML hiring grew 20% and auto rose 11%. BPO/ITES and GCC each rose 4%, while IT/software services, pharma/biotech and FMCG each fell 4%, and healthcare fell 3%. Hyderabad led the cities at 9% growth. Delhi-NCR and Mumbai each fell 6%. Info Edge CEO Hitesh Oberoi, quoted by Staffing Industry Analysts, called the market 'steady, but more selective'. For jobseekers in IT and metros, the numbers show demand concentrated in AI skills and a few cities.

title: Infosys adds 4,480 employees in Q2 FY27, hires over 8,000 freshers
body: Infosys' headcount reached 332,542 at the end of September 2026, a net addition of 4,480 in the quarter after a decline of 532 in Q1. It hired more than 8,000 freshers in Q2, on top of more than 4,000 in Q1, against a full-year target of about 20,000. Trailing attrition fell to 12.7% from 13%. The company cut its FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1%–2% from 1.5%–3%. The page does not discuss wage hikes, which many Infosys staff have been waiting on. Hiring is up even as the company trims its growth outlook.

title: Wipro workforce declines 2.8% sequentially to 236,328 in Q2 FY27
body: Wipro's headcount fell by 6,716, or about 2.8%, to 236,328 in the September 2026 quarter, from 243,044 in Q1. Net utilisation was 83.4%, against 86.4% a year earlier. Voluntary attrition was 13.8%. Another outlet, The People's Board (also dated 16 October 2026), quotes CHRO Saurabh Govil: 'We are going back to the campuses now in H2 to hire.' He added that headcount 'will keep going up and down'. This contrasts with TCS, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra, which all added staff in the same quarter. People Matters notes the data does not explain the reasons for the drop.

title: Tech Mahindra adds nearly 5,500 employees in Q2, highest quarterly addition in two years
body: Tech Mahindra added nearly 5,500 employees in the September 2026 quarter. It was the first quarterly addition in four quarters and the largest in two years. Total headcount reached 1.52 lakh, above the Bloomberg consensus of 1.49 lakh. Trailing attrition was 11.7%, against 12.8% a year earlier. Employee costs rose 4.5% year on year to ₹8,232 crore. The page lists peers' moves as HCL Technologies +6,450, TCS nearly +4,300 and Wipro about -6,700. The IT job market is mixed, with some firms hiring again while Wipro cuts.

title: HCLTech attrition rises to 12.8% as headcount grows by 6,450 in Q2
body: HCLTech's headcount rose by 6,450 to 2,30,339 in the September 2026 quarter. It onboarded 6,136 freshers, about 1,000 more than in Q2 FY26, and about 15% of them were in the 'elite engineer' category. Voluntary attrition edged up to 12.8% from 12.7%. Revenue per employee was $65,400, against $65,500 in June. The article says the data 'does not establish the reasons behind the change in attrition'. For fresher candidates, it shows one large IT firm hiring more campus talent.

title: Indian companies project 9.1% salary hikes in 2027, up from 9% in 2026 (Aon survey)
body: Aon's Annual Salary Increase and Turnover Survey for India 2026-27 covers 1,200+ organisations across 45 industries. It projects a 9.1% salary increase in 2027, up from 9% in 2026. Technology consulting and services is lowest at 6.6%, and NBFCs are highest at 10.1%. Attrition rose to 18% in 2026 from 16.2% in 2025, and involuntary attrition rose to 4% from 3.4%. AI productivity tool adoption reached 56% in 2026, up from 46.1% in 2025, and AI/ML/data science talent premiums rose about 10%. IT services staff are again at the bottom of the pay table while AI skills command a premium.

title: Infosys chairman calls job fears 'hogwash' as AI spurs business
body: At the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Infosys Chairman Nandan Nilekani dismissed fears that AI will eliminate jobs, calling the idea 'hogwash'. He said: 'We are going to see only more work coming our way'. He acknowledged coding is 'getting automated' but said governance, change management and guardrails make up 70% of a transformation project. Infosys shares are down about 45% over two years but rose 3.2% on 13 October. The article carries no worker reactions; it sits against surveys showing AI-related job anxiety among Indian workers.

title: Indian IT services hiring hits high: Naukri-linked white-collar data, Hyderabad and Chennai lead
body: Staffing Industry Analysts reports that September 2026 hiring was up 2% year on year (index 3,053 vs 3,002). AI and ML roles rose 20% and the auto sector 11%, while education fell 18% and telecom 12%. By experience, hiring for 0–3 years rose 1%, 4–7 years fell 2%, 8–12 years rose 5%, 13–15 years rose 7% and 16+ years rose 5%. Info Edge CEO Hitesh Oberoi said the market is 'steady, but more selective'. For mid-career workers with 4–7 years of experience, demand is slightly down, while senior hands are in more demand.

title: Instagram tests 90-minute 'Features' videos, but Indian creators can't use it yet
body: Instagram is testing a long-form format called Features. It allows horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes for selected creators. The test began in Brazil and is expanding to a small group in the US, and the article says Indian creators should not assume they have access. YouTube's Partner Programme gives eligible creators 55% of net ad revenue. Meta says it is 'too early to share a long-term monetization model'. Instagram head Adam Mosseri said, 'I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram.' The article advises creators to keep full-length videos on YouTube and to track watch time and repeat viewers, not just views.

title: Facebook tests opening straight into Reels for users in India
body: Meta is testing a Facebook layout in India that opens into full-screen video. Users in the test can opt out to a Feed-first view, and the classic feed stays as a second tab. Meta's ad tools indicate a Facebook audience of 400+ million in India, its largest market by users. Meta-commissioned studies say 89% of Gen Z respondents use Reels every day. The article quotes no users, so reaction is not covered, only Meta's framing that Reels is India's 'personal and primary screen'.

title: 'No SIM, no WhatsApp': SIM-binding rule has users and experts asking if it can work
body: The Department of Telecommunications has told messaging apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram to keep accounts linked to an active SIM in the device. The compliance deadline is now December 31, 2026. The article cites about ₹22,848 crore in cyber-fraud losses in 2024. A cited survey found that 80% of consumers and over 60% of small businesses expect disruption. Experts doubt the tech works: ex-Qualcomm India executive Parag Kar called continuous SIM validation infeasible, and Pranesh Prakash questioned whether it would cut fraud. The telecom industry body COAI backs it. Concerns include people using tablets, secondary phones or computers.

title: Viral claim that Meta will shut Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp in India is misleading
body: A viral post, started by Kamal R Khan, shared an image reading 'We Will Exit India if Forced to Break Encryption'. It led many people to think the apps were about to go dark. The fact-check found no new announcement from Meta. The line goes back to 2024, when WhatsApp told the Delhi High Court it could stop operating in India if forced to break end-to-end encryption. Online reaction was mixed. Some said WhatsApp should protect privacy, while others questioned the government's traceability rules.

title: Indian travel YouTuber with no money pushed out of a Thai temple, and viewers pile on
body: Banshi, an Indian travel YouTuber with about 17,300 subscribers, said he was travelling in Thailand without money and tried to sleep at a temple in Udon Thani. Police asked him to leave and offered help reaching a budget hotel at about 400 baht per night, which he declined. He moved to a petrol station instead. Many commenters criticised him for travelling without enough funds and expecting free stays. Some praised the officers for handling it politely. Some Indians living in Thailand said such behaviour reinforces negative stereotypes about Indian tourists.

title: YouTube-commissioned report: India's creator ecosystem supports 9.6 lakh jobs
body: An Oxford Economics report for YouTube says the ecosystem supported 9.6 lakh+ full-time equivalent jobs and added ₹18,000 crore+ to GDP in 2025. 18,000+ Indian channels have passed 1 million subscribers. Six-figure-revenue channels rose 30%+ year on year. About 73% of monetising creators say YouTube is their primary income source. The report says job growth is spreading to hubs like Jaipur, Lucknow and Kochi. This is YouTube's own commissioned study, and the article quotes no creators or analysts.

title: Flipkart seller's handwritten 'Please don't return' note goes viral
body: On October 24, X user @dev_kalpeshkk posted a handwritten note found with a delivered T-shirt. It read, 'Please don't return the product, sir. I am already running at a loss… PLEASE NO RETURN.' Many users worried about small sellers, since returns add costs and returned clothes can be hard to resell. One user pointed to customers who return clothes after wearing them. Others guessed the seller was under financial strain, though that is unverified. The talk widened to marketplace return policies and what small sellers absorb.

title: Aakash Chopra memed after '170+ tough to chase' post before India's record chase
body: Before the 3rd T20I against New Zealand, Aakash Chopra posted that '170+ will be a tough chase today'. New Zealand made 198/3, and India chased it in 13.2 overs with six wickets and 40 balls to spare. Abhishek Sharma made 113 off 38 balls and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 45 off 19. India's 118 in the powerplay beat the previous best of 116. Fans flooded X with memes. One said, 'Completed in 10 over tell me next.' Others joked it was a T10 match and asked him to delete the post.

title: Viral video of guards pushing devotees at Dharashiv's Tulja Bhavani temple sparks outrage
body: A video from October 26 allegedly shows Maharashtra Security Force personnel pushing and rough-handling devotees inside the sanctum of Shri Tulja Bhavani Temple. Devotees had reportedly waited in long queues. People on X condemned it and criticised VIP darshan practices, saying ordinary devotees should not be treated as obstacles. Some tagged the Maharashtra Chief Minister and asked for action. The temple had not issued a statement, and the claims rest on the video and social media reaction.

title: Instagram withholds news creators' accounts in India; four restored after legal notices
body: The Internet Freedom Foundation says journalists and news creators covering protests have had posts or accounts withheld in India. Restricted users saw a notice that Meta acted 'pursuant to legal requirements' under the IT Rules, naming no provision or post. Four accounts were restored on 19–20 October after legal notices sent on 15 October. They had about 4.7 lakh, 1.05 lakh, 37,900 and 5.36 lakh followers. Each complaint was closed in 2–4 minutes, with only generic replies. The IFF says, 'Free speech cannot be muffled as a precaution.' One account was withheld again a day before publication.

title: Gen Z fashion influencers reportedly earn ₹2–7 lakh per 15-second reel
body: AajTak reports that Gen Z beauty and fashion influencers make 15–30 second Instagram and YouTube videos. It says the top five earn ₹2 lakh to ₹7 lakh per branded reel. Komal Pandey is put at ₹4–6 lakh per reel and Kritika Khurana at ₹3–5 lakh. Brand endorsements are about 70% of earnings, and affiliate links add 5%–15% commission. The rate figures are not attributed to the creators or verified, and no creators are quoted. The piece feeds the 'reels as a career' conversation.

title: North Indian influencer's Fort Kochi video triggers Kerala backlash; Diya Krishna's comment adds fuel
body: Influencer Amrit Singh Darren posted a video about Kashi Art Cafe in Fort Kochi. He objected to a Jinnah portrait and beef on the menu, and claimed about 95% of local businesses are Muslim-run, a figure the article does not verify. Malayalis pushed back online against his portrayal of the area. Influencer Diya Krishna commented 'Sad reality', then deleted it. She said she meant only the portrait and had not watched the second half of the video. She said she was heartbroken by the hurtful messages and urged people to stop creating controversy. The article says the criticism has continued.

title: Drishyam: The Conclusion opens to a mostly warm reception on X
body: Ajay Devgn's Hindi Drishyam: The Conclusion opened on 2 October. Viewers on X praised the tension, the interval sequence and the climax. They also praised Ajay Devgn's restrained acting and Jaideep Ahlawat's intensity. One viewer said the twist was "BETTER than Drishyam 1 and 2", and others found it stronger than the Malayalam original. Taran Adarsh gave it 4.5 stars, but one viewer gave 1.5 stars. Some called the story predictable and questioned whether it matched the earlier films' emotional weight. One fan predicted it would cross ₹600 crore, which is a fan's forecast, not a reported figure.

title: Drishyam 3 is in its fourth week and has crossed ₹371 crore net
body: By Day 26, Tuesday 27 October, the film had earned ₹371.20 Cr India net and ₹576.35 Cr worldwide gross. Weekly India net ran ₹245.50 Cr in week 1, ₹87.50 Cr in week 2 and ₹28.85 Cr in week 3. Day 26 added ₹1.25 Cr, up 19.0% from ₹1.05 Cr on Day 25, on overall occupancy of 15.31%. The page lists no audience verdict. A related headline notes Mohanlal publicly praised the film and its different ending. The run is a huge win that is now settling into a long tail.

title: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to win Asian Games men's cricket gold
body: India won the men's final in Nisshin, Japan, after batting first and making 211/6 in 20 overs. Pakistan finished on 192/6. Abhishek Sharma hit 61 off 28 balls with seven sixes, and Tilak Varma made 51 not out off 22. Captain Shreyas Iyer made 21 off 24 balls. The page carries no fan reactions. It was a gold-medal clash against Pakistan that Indian fans were always going to watch closely.

title: Gajab Raat: the Manoj Bajpayee film renamed after the Ghooskhor Pandat title row
body: The Netflix film was first titled Ghooskhor Pandat. Critics and groups said the title derisively linked a community to corruption. In February 2026 the UP Police filed an FIR in Lucknow. The Supreme Court said "freedom of speech cannot be used as a licence to denigrate a section of society." Producer Neeraj Pandey filed an affidavit withdrawing the title, and the film became Gajab Raat, premiering 23 October. Manoj Bajpayee backed the change. He also condemned online toxicity aimed at his family and said the film does not represent any caste, religion or community.

title: Gajab Raat review: Bajpayee holds a one-night Netflix thriller together
body: Free Press Journal gave Ritesh Shah's debut 3.5 stars. It praised Bajpayee's performance as a compromised policeman, the humorous exchanges with Rajiv Gupta, and the single-night setting that keeps up the pace. It also praised the film's point that ordinary citizens bear the cost of decisions made in power. It faulted the predictable revelations, the broadly sketched characters and the thin roles for Divya Dutta, Akshay Oberoi and Saqib Saleem. Kiku Sharda is underused. The verdict is that it may not reinvent the genre but is engaging.

title: Vvaan opens at ₹33.25 crore despite harsh reviews, Sidharth Malhotra's best weekend since 2015
body: The fantasy thriller made ₹8 crore on Friday, ₹11.25 crore on Saturday and ₹14 crore on Sunday. That is ₹33.25 crore net in three days, with ₹43.15 crore worldwide. The article says reviewers were almost unanimous in dismissing it. Ticket buyers disagreed, and daily collections kept rising, which it credits to positive word of mouth. Sacnilk's Day 16 page later showed ₹67.35 Cr India net. Viewers on X were split. Praise went to the folklore and Chhath Puja setting and to Sunil Grover, while others criticised the slow first half and weak visuals.

title: West Indies beat India by 24 runs in Hyderabad as Shai Hope hits a hundred
body: West Indies made 247-3 and won the fourth T20I, levelling the series at 2-2. Shai Hope was unbeaten on 102 off 50 balls, with nine sixes. India were all out for 223 in 19.3 overs, having been 130-5 at one stage. Sanju Samson made 56 off 23 balls. Keemo Paul took 5-41. Al Jazeera says it was the second-highest first-innings total in T20s against India. The page carries no fan reactions.

title: Rain ends the India–West Indies T20I decider in Bengaluru, series shared 2-2
body: The fifth T20I on 17 October was abandoned after India reached 118 for 5 in 7.4 overs. West Indies had a DLS target of 84 in five overs, but more rain stopped the chase. Ishan Kishan made 30 off 10 balls. West Indies finished with a series run rate of 10.98, which the article reports as the highest by any Full Member team in a bilateral T20I series. They hit 105 sixes. The article notes that supporters were frustrated and that the Bengaluru crowd missed a decisive finish, without quoting anyone.

title: Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi concert: permission refused, then granted within a day
body: On 22 October Delhi Police refused permission for Diljit's Aura Tour show at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on 30 October, citing security and law-and-order concerns. On 23 October BookMyShow confirmed the show would go ahead. It said permission was reconsidered and issued after it submitted a plan on security and crowd management. Delhi is one stop on a seven-city tour. The article does not describe fan reaction to the Delhi decision. It notes only that the internet has been flooded with hate comments about Dosanjh in general.

title: Ayushmann's Udta Teer opens at just ₹4.10 crore
body: The spy comedy made ₹4.10 crore India net on Friday 23 October from 6,265 shows, with 13% overall occupancy. That is about 83% below his best opener, Thamma, at ₹24 crore. Footfalls were about 1,87,849. Sacnilk's own analysis blames limited pre-release buzz, an unconventional premise and competition from Nayyi Navelli, Prahaar and Jailer 2. The page has no audience or critic quotes. A later Sacnilk list showed ₹27.21 Cr India gross.

title: Nayyi Navelli edges past Prahaar in a Dussehra clash despite mixed reviews
body: Yami Gautam's film earned ₹3.25 Cr, ₹4.00 Cr and ₹4.40 Cr over its opening weekend, a total of ₹11.65 Cr net. Rajkummar Rao's Prahaar made ₹9.15 Cr, so Nayyi Navelli finished ₹2.50 Cr ahead. Occupancy rose from 11% to 17% by Sunday. Critics were mixed. Some praised Yami and the family humour, while others questioned the screenplay and the mythological elements. Yami thanked audiences for celebrating Dussehra with a film that "brings families together in cinemas".

title: Jailer 2 opens with ₹125.25 crore worldwide; ₹477.75 crore by Day 5
body: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 made ₹59.7 crore net in India on Day 1 and ₹37.1 crore on Day 2. It made ₹47.25 crore on Day 3 and ₹55.85 crore on Day 4. Day 5 was about ₹39.95 crore as of 10 pm, and the five-day India net was ₹239.85 crore. Worldwide gross reached ₹477.75 crore by Day 5. Day 5 was the biggest first Monday for a Tamil film, ahead of Leo's ₹39.5 crore. The article quotes no viewers and only says the film is still luring fans to theatres. Hollywood Reporter India's review called it a "hilariously dark sequel" that "eventually settles for safety".

title: Delhi bars non-BS6 outside vehicles from November 1 under Winter Action Plan
body: Delhi's Winter Action Plan runs from November 1, 2026 to January 31. Vehicles registered outside Delhi that don't meet BS6 standards will be barred from entering the capital, and ANPR cameras at the borders will spot them. The Transport Department estimates over 10 lakh vehicles in the NCR could be affected, including about 2 lakh non-BS6 vehicles in Gurugram and Faridabad and nearly 4 lakh in Ghaziabad. Delhi-registered pre-BS6 vehicles need a valid PUCC or they cannot buy fuel. The page quotes no commuter reactions and does not confirm the fine, only that a 'hefty challan' is possible. Owners can check their emission standard on the RC or the mParivahan app.

title: Caller name display (CNAP) goes live on 4G+ networks on 1 November; new spam-call rules already in force
body: From 1 November 2026, caller name display (CNAP) starts on 4G and higher networks, under a DoT circular dated 13 October 2026. CNAP for 2G, 3G and landlines has no date yet. Stage 1 of TRAI's amended calling rules went live around 18 October. Operators now flag suspected spam numbers, and five or more flags within 10 days trigger graded action. FULLY BLOCK preferences move to BLOCK PROMO within 15 days. A stage 2 on about 17 November adds an A2P termination charge of up to ₹0.05 per minute for automated calls. The page is a explainer and reports no public reaction.

title: Jewellers push rate-locking and advance booking before Dhanteras as gold sits near ₹1.42–1.44 lakh
body: Dhanteras falls on November 6, 2026, and gold trades at about Rs. 1.42–1.44 lakh per 10 grams, with silver at about Rs. 1.95–1.96 lakh per kg. Kalyan Jewellers and Joyalukkas offer advance-booking schemes so buyers can fix today's price. Sales were weak during Dussehra. Senco says old-gold exchanges are more than 50% of its business. High prices are pushing some shoppers toward lightweight jewellery and old-gold trade-ins. Senco expects festive growth above 20%, and Kataria Jewellers expects Dhanteras sales up 35–40% on 2025. These are retailer forecasts, not shopper quotes.

title: Delhi-NCR Diwali firecracker rules still unsettled, Supreme Court leans toward a time-limited middle path
body: At a 30 September 2026 hearing, the Supreme Court bench said a complete ban could hurt the sentiments of people celebrating, while all-day bursting would harm vulnerable groups. It favoured time limits and seemed inclined to allow joint crackers ('laris') with conditions, reversing last year's ban. A decision is due after a CPCB report on barium crackers, expected by 15 October. Last year's order allowed only NEERI-approved green crackers, from 6–7 am and 8–10 pm. Diwali 2026 falls on 8 November. The page carries no resident reaction. It reflects the position as of 5 October, and I did not find the final ruling.

title: Match Group–Ipsos survey: 35% of Indian singles feel lonely, 58% have wide online circles but feel lonely in person
body: The survey covered 1,000 singles aged 18 to 45 in metro and tier-1 cities. About 35% say they constantly feel lonely, and about 58% connect widely online but feel lonely in person. About 55% are too tired after work to meet or talk to anyone, and 64% put studies and jobs ahead of their social lives. About 72% prefer a few deep connections to many casual friends. About 85% want long-term relationships (89% among Gen Z), and 63% would wait rather than settle. About 40% use dating apps, and 60% worry about safety in online dating. Match Group's regional head said close relationships are harder to build in a fast-paced lifestyle.

title: EPFO wage ceiling raised from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000: what it means for take-home
body: The EPFO wage ceiling rises from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month, and contributions are calculated on PF wages, not gross salary. At PF wages of ₹20,000, the employee EPF contribution is ₹2,400 a month. At ₹25,000 it is ₹3,000. At ₹35,000 it is capped at ₹3,000 rather than ₹4,200. Employers contribute the same share. The article is an explainer for employees on how their deductions change. It reports no reactions.

title: Retail inflation rises to 5.54% in September; onion inflation crosses 108%
body: Combined CPI inflation was 5.54% in September 2026, up from 4.83% in August. Rural inflation was 6.08% and urban 4.88%. Food inflation (CFPI) rose to 7.74% from 5.97%. Onion inflation jumped to 108.09% from 48.78% in August, while potato (-11.50%) and tomato (-8.62%) prices fell. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services had the highest division inflation, at 13.75%. The page is a data summary and does not quote consumers.

title: RBI hikes repo rate 25 bps to 5.50%; home-loan EMIs set to rise
body: The RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7, 2026, the first hike since February 2023. For a 20-year home loan at 7.50% going to 7.75%, EMIs rise by Rs 307 on ₹20 lakh (Rs 16,112 to Rs 16,419), Rs 460 on ₹30 lakh (Rs 24,168 to Rs 24,628) and nearly Rs 767 on ₹50 lakh (Rs 40,280 to Rs 41,047). The article calls these approximate and says the impact depends on the lender, benchmark and remaining tenure. Borrowers with floating-rate loans are the ones affected. It carries no borrower quotes.

title: Rupee near record low of 96.97 as forex reserves fall to $734 billion
body: The rupee was about 0.2% from its record low of 96.97 per dollar, set in May 2026, and has fallen more than 7% in 2026. Forex reserves were $734 billion in the week ended Oct 2, down from a record $785 billion in the week ended Sept 4. Foreign investors have sold almost $30 billion of Indian equities this year. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra put import cover at about 11 months. Analysts expect a 96–98 range in the second half of the fiscal year. The page reports market views, not ordinary consumers' reactions.

title: Delhi GRAP 1: parking fees double, no fuel without PUC, staggered hours for government staff
body: Delhi's AQI rose from 179 on 20 October to 244 on 21 October 2026, putting the city in the GRAP 1 'Poor' band (AQI 201–300). Parking fees double at city-owned lots, though the page is unclear whether this covers all of them or excludes Metro parking. Vehicles without a valid PUC certificate get no fuel. DMRC adds weekday trips from 22 October. Delhi government and MCD staff get staggered hours and work-from-home, while private employers decide for themselves. The page notes no general stay-at-home rule for private-sector staff and reports no worker reactions.

title: Navratri car registrations fall 22% on last year's GST-cut base, but Maruti reports 35% retail growth
body: Dealers' body FADA reported passenger-vehicle retail sales during Navratri fell 22% year-on-year, from 2,34,004 units to 1,82,728. Last year's base was inflated by the GST cuts effective September 22, 2025. Maruti Suzuki said retail sales from Ganesh Chaturthi to Dussehra rose 35%, with SUVs roughly doubling and pending bookings up from about 2 lakh to 2.7 lakh. Hyundai registrations to Navratri rose about 30% to nearly 41,000 units. The page reflects dealer and carmaker views, not buyer comments.

title: GST changes from November 1: late-fee waiver, faster refunds and small-seller relief
body: Measures that need no legislative change may start November 1, 2026, and the rest are targeted for April 1, 2027. Late fees are waived for taxpayers with turnover up to ₹5 crore who file delayed returns by the end of the month they were due. Zero-rated supply and inverted-duty refund claims could get 90% provisional refunds. Officials said nearly 80% of GST notices stem from return mismatches. Show-cause notices would carry a minimum aggregate tax threshold of ₹10,000. The 57th GST Council meeting on October 8 focused on compliance, not rate changes. This mainly affects small businesses and sellers, and the page reports no reactions.
